conditions_text: Indian passport holders who also hold a valid US visa or Green Card (or a UK/EU residence visa) can get a UAE visa on arrival. The document must have at least 6 months' validity remaining.
fee_notes: Free on arrival under this route; one extension of 14 days available for a fee (AED 250).

conditions_text: Without a qualifying US/UK/EU (or Australia/Canada/Japan/South Korea/Singapore/New Zealand residence) document, Indian passport holders must arrange a UAE visa in advance.
Indian nationals holding a valid US, UK, Irish, or Schengen visa or residence permit are eligible for Turkey's e-Visa, single entry, applied for online.
fee_notes: Paid e-visa, applied for online in advance.

conditions_text: Turkey does not offer visa on arrival for Indian passport holders. Without a qualifying US/UK/Irish/Schengen visa, a sticker visa from a Turkish mission is required.

Indian nationals holding a valid, unexpired US visa (any type) or US permanent residence (Green Card) are exempt from obtaining a separate Mexican visa for tourism, business, or transit entry. The FMM (Forma Migratoria Múltiple) tourist permit is completed on arrival — printed and presented at land border crossings, or issued digitally at international airports.
fee_notes: FMM tourist permit fee applies (~$57 USD / ~983 MXN); length of stay granted is at the immigration officer's discretion, up to this maximum. Land entries of 7 days or less are typically fee-exempt.

conditions_text: Without a qualifying valid visa or permanent residence document from the US, Canada, UK, Japan, or a Schengen Area country, Indian nationals must obtain a Mexican visa in advance from a Mexican embassy or consulate before traveling.

Indian nationals (Costa Rica's Group III, consular-visa-required) may enter without a separate Costa Rican visa if they hold a valid multiple-entry U.S. visa or U.S. residency permit (any category, including refugee/asylum status, and visa types D or C1/D only — transit visas C1/C2/C3 do not qualify) with at least 1 day of remaining validity. The same exception applies with a valid multiple-entry Canadian visa or residency. The stay authorized on arrival cannot exceed the remaining validity of that U.S./Canadian document, as determined by the immigration officer at entry.

India is listed in Group III ("visa consular") of Costa Rica's official visa directive. Without a qualifying multiple-entry U.S./Canadian visa or residency (see the held-document exception), Indian nationals must obtain a Costa Rican consular visa in advance: single entry only, must be stamped within 3 months of approval, and once stamped must be used to enter Costa Rica within 60 business days. Passport must be valid at least 180 days.
fee_notes: Initial stamp is typically 30 days; extendable to a total of 90 days from within Costa Rica, per the directive's Group III terms.

conditions_text: Georgia grants visa-free entry to holders of a valid visa or residence permit from the US, UK, Japan, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Israel, South Korea, Ireland, Schengen, or GCC countries.
Indian passport holders without a qualifying third-country visa can apply for Georgia's standard e-visa.
fee_notes: Paid e-visa, applied for online.

conditions_text: Armenia grants visa on arrival at the border to Indian passport holders who present a valid visa or residence permit issued by the US, any EU/Schengen member state, the UK, Australia, Canada, Japan, New Zealand, South Korea, Russia, or the Gulf states (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain, Oman).

Indian nationals without a qualifying third-country visa or residence permit can apply for Armenia's e-visa online via the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' e-visa portal (evisa.mfa.am), which requires travel insurance plus either a qualifying third-country visa/residence permit or a return ticket, invitation letter, and proof of sufficient funds.
A valid US, UK, EU, or Schengen visa or residence permit substitutes for a Serbian visa entirely, for up to 90 days in any 180-day period.
Without a qualifying third-country visa, Indian nationals can apply for Serbia's e-visa for the same 90-day allowance.

Since 8 June 2025, Indian nationals travelling to the Philippines for tourism or business may enter without a visa for a non-extendible, non-convertible period of 14 days, provided they hold a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the contemplated stay, a confirmed hotel booking, proof of financial capacity, and a return or onward ticket, and have no derogatory record with the Bureau of Immigration.

Since 8 June 2025, Indian nationals holding a valid, current American, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore, or UK (AJACSSUK) visa or residence permit may enter the Philippines visa-free for a non-extendible period of 30 days for tourism or business, instead of the standard 14 days, provided their passport is valid at least 6 months beyond the contemplated stay and they hold a return or onward ticket to their next destination.

Indian nationals may enter Colombia without a Colombian visa if, at the time of entry, they hold a valid US visa (other than an airport-transit visa) with at least 180 days' remaining validity, or a valid US residence permit. This is a conditional visa exemption under Colombia's Resolucion 5488 of 2022, Article 3 Literal C (as amended by Resolucion 3717 of 2023).

Indian nationals who do not hold a qualifying US or Schengen visa (or a residence permit in the US or a Schengen state) do not fall under Colombia's conditional visa exemption (Resolucion 5488 of 2022, Article 3 Literal C) and must obtain a Colombian visa in advance from a Colombian consulate before travel (Article 7), applied for online through the Cancilleria's e-visa portal (visas.cancilleria.gov.co).
Indian nationals holding a valid US, UK, Canada, Australia, or Schengen visa or permanent resident permit (minimum 6 months' validity) can stay visa-free for tourism or business.
fee_notes: Up to 180 days within any 365-day period.

conditions_text: Without a qualifying US/UK/Canada/Australia/Schengen document, Indian nationals must obtain a Peruvian visa in advance.

Indian passport holders can obtain Indonesia's Visitor Visa (electronic visa on arrival / e-VOA) online via the official evisa.imigrasi.go.id portal, applied for before or on arrival, for tourism, business meetings, government visits, goods purchasing, or transit; independent of any other visa held. Passport must be valid for at least 6 months.
fee_notes: IDR 500,000 (approx. $32 USD), paid online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id by Visa/Mastercard/JCB credit card; one 30-day extension is possible (total maximum 60 days), processed through the same portal or an immigration office.

conditions_text: The Maldives grants visa-free entry on arrival to virtually all nationalities. Indian nationals specifically get 90 days (most nationalities get 30) under a bilateral reciprocity arrangement.

Sri Lanka requires an ETA (Electronic Travel Authorization) for Indian nationals, applied for online at eta.gov.lk. Since 25 May 2026 the ETA is free of charge for Indian passport holders, with double-entry allowed within the validity window.
fee_notes: Free as of 25 May 2026 (previously ~$20 USD). Extendable up to a total of 270 days from within Sri Lanka.

conditions_text: US passport holders are unilaterally exempt from any visa requirement to enter Armenia and may stay for up to 180 days per calendar year, per Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of unilaterally visa-exempt countries.

No visa needed for tourism stays of up to 90 days, per Colombia's Resolucion 5488 of 2022 (Article 3, Literal A, which lists Estados Unidos de America among nationalities exempt from the short-stay visa requirement). A one-time extension (Permiso Temporal de Permanencia) can bring the total to a maximum of 180 days, continuous or discontinuous, within the same calendar year, per Migracion Colombia's Resolucion 2061 of 2020.

The United States is in Group I (visa-free) of Costa Rica's official visa directive. The immigration officer sets the authorized stay on arrival, up to a maximum of 180 calendar days, generally non-extendable (an initial grant of under 90 days may be extended to a total of 90 days).
A full year visa-free — one of the most generous allowances Georgia grants.

US passport holders can obtain Indonesia's Visitor Visa (electronic visa on arrival / e-VOA) online via the official evisa.imigrasi.go.id portal; single-entry, for tourism, business meetings, government visits, goods purchasing, or transit. Passport must be valid for at least 6 months.
fee_notes: IDR 500,000 (approx. $33 USD), paid online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id by Visa/Mastercard/JCB credit card; one 30-day extension is possible (total maximum 60 days), processed through the same portal or an immigration office.

conditions_text: Free visa on arrival, extendable up to 90 days.
fee_notes: Free.

conditions_text: US citizens do not need a visa for tourism, business, or transit stays. A Forma Migratoria Múltiple (FMM) is required for all visitors: land entrants must complete, print, and present the FMM at the immigration checkpoint; air travelers receive a digital FMM (FMMd) automatically as part of arrival processing.
fee_notes: Included in airfare for air arrivals; FMM fee (~$54-57 USD / ~983 MXN) applies for land entries staying over 7 days, payable at the INM checkpoint or online.

conditions_text: No visa needed for tourism.

US nationals may enter the Philippines without a visa for tourism or business for an initial stay of up to 30 days under Executive Order 408 (as amended), provided they hold a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the contemplated stay and a return or onward ticket to their next destination.
90 days within any 180-day period.

Sri Lanka requires an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) for US nationals, applied for online at eta.gov.lk before arrival. Since 25 May 2026 the tourist ETA is free of charge for US passport holders as one of 40 eligible nationalities, with double-entry permitted within the 30-day validity window from the date of first arrival. This is a free ETA requirement, not full visa-free entry -- an ETA application before travel remains mandatory.
fee_notes: Free as of 25 May 2026 (previously a paid ETA). Stays beyond 30 days require a separate extension at the applicable fee, arranged with the Department of Immigration and Emigration.

conditions_text: 90 days within any 180-day period, tourism purpose only.

A visa is issued free of charge upon arrival, allowing a maximum stay of 90 days, whether continuous or intermittent, within 180 days calculated from the date of first entry; this 90-day allowance is explicitly non-renewable. A passport valid for at least 6 months beyond arrival and a round-trip or onward ticket are required. Overstaying incurs a fine of AED 50 per day.

UK passport holders are unilaterally exempt from any visa requirement to enter Armenia (not merely visa-on-arrival) and may stay for up to 180 days per calendar year, per Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of unilaterally visa-exempt countries.

No visa needed for tourism stays of up to 90 days, per Colombia's Resolucion 5488 of 2022 (Article 3, Literal A, which lists Reino Unido de la Gran Bretana e Irlanda del Norte among nationalities exempt from the short-stay visa requirement). A one-time extension (Permiso Temporal de Permanencia) can bring the total to a maximum of 180 days, continuous or discontinuous, within the same calendar year, per Migracion Colombia's Resolucion 2061 of 2020.

The United Kingdom (England, Wales, Scotland, and Northern Ireland) is in Group I (visa-free) of Costa Rica's official visa directive. The exact period is at the discretion of the immigration officer on arrival, up to a maximum of 180 calendar days, generally non-extendable (an initial grant of under 90 days may be extended to a total of 90 days).
A full year visa-free.

UK passport holders can obtain Indonesia's Visitor Visa (electronic visa on arrival / e-VOA) online via the official evisa.imigrasi.go.id portal; single-entry, for tourism, business meetings, government visits, goods purchasing, or transit. Passport must be valid for at least 6 months.
fee_notes: IDR 500,000 (approx. £25), paid online via evisa.imigrasi.go.id by Visa/Mastercard/JCB credit card; one 30-day extension is possible (total maximum 60 days), processed through the same portal or an immigration office.

conditions_text: Free visa on arrival.
fee_notes: Free.

conditions_text: British citizens do not need a visa for tourism. Stay length is granted via the FMM and/or stamped on arrival, up to 180 days. Travelers entering by land must complete an FMM (in-person/printed at the border); air travelers receive a digital FMM automatically. No paid or voluntary work is permitted under this status.
Up to 183 accumulated days within a 365-day period.

British passport holders may enter the Philippines without a visa for tourism or business for an initial stay of up to 30 days under Executive Order 408 (as amended), provided they hold a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the contemplated stay and a return or onward ticket. For stays longer than 30 days, a 9(a) Temporary Visitor visa can be obtained in advance from the Philippine Embassy in London.
No visa needed for tourism.

fee_notes: Free as of 25 May 2026 (previously a paid ETA). Stays beyond 30 days require a separate extension at the applicable fee, arranged with the Department of Immigration and Emigration.

A visitor visa is issued free of charge on arrival and stamped into the passport, allowing a stay of up to 90 days within a 180-day period beginning from the date of first entry (stay may be continuous or split across multiple visits). No advance application is needed. To extend, contact the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (in Dubai) or the Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs & Port Security (rest of the UAE) before the visa expires; overstaying incurs accumulating daily fines.

German passport holders are on Armenia's unilateral visa-exemption list and may enter for tourism, business, or family visits without a visa. Stay is capped at 180 days per calendar year, and longer stays or employment require a residence application before that period expires.

German citizens do not need a visa for purely touristic stays in Colombia; immigration stamps an initial permitted stay of up to 90 days on arrival, which can be extended once by a further 90 days at Migración Colombia's discretion. Travelers must also complete the free online Check-Mig pre-registration within 72 hours before each flight.

German citizens do not need a visa for tourist entry to Costa Rica and may be granted up to 180 days on arrival, though immigration officers can grant a shorter period based on return ticket, funds, and stated purpose. A passport valid at least 6 months beyond the stay and proof of onward travel are required.

German citizens may enter and stay in Georgia for up to 360 days without a visa; a residence permit must be obtained at a Public Service Hall before this period expires for longer stays. Since 1 January 2026, entrants must also show proof of health/travel insurance covering the whole stay with minimum coverage of 30,000 GEL.

German citizens can obtain a paid visa-on-arrival (or the equivalent electronic e-VOA applied for online in advance) at Indonesian entry points for tourism, valid up to 30 days with one 30-day extension available online. A passport valid at least 6 months and a return/onward ticket are required; volunteer or paid work is not permitted on this visa.
fee_notes: IDR 500,000 paid in cash at the airport, or paid online in advance for the electronic version (e-VOA).

conditions_text: German tourists receive a free 30-day visa on arrival in the Maldives after completing the mandatory IMUGA online entry declaration within 96 hours before arrival. An extension to a total of 90 days is possible but must be applied for locally and requires a recommendation from the resort/hotel.
fee_notes: Free for the initial 30-day visa on arrival; extension to 90 days is a separate paid, in-country application.

conditions_text: German citizens do not need a visa for tourism, transit, or business (without taking up employment) in Mexico as long as the stay does not exceed 180 days; the actual number of days granted is set by the immigration officer at entry and stamped in the passport (or noted on the FMM tourist card).

German citizens do not need a visa for tourist stays in Peru of up to 90 days per half-year; the exact permitted duration is not guaranteed to be the full 90 days and depends on information given at entry. Overstaying incurs a fine of 5 Peruvian soles per day before departure.

German tourists receive a fee-free 30-day visa waiver on arrival in the Philippines upon presenting a valid return or onward flight ticket; a further extension to a maximum of 59 total days is possible through the Bureau of Immigration. Pre-arrival online registration via the government's eTravel portal (etravel.gov.ph) is required, producing a QR code that airlines check at check-in.

German citizens do not need a visa for tourist entry to Serbia and may stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period; time spent in Kosovo counts toward this same 90-day limit under Serbian rules. Longer stays or employment require a residence permit applied for in advance or after arrival at the local foreign police office.

German citizens must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) before traveling to Sri Lanka via the official eta.gov.lk portal; it is issued as a single-entry tourist authorization for an initial 30 days. Since 25 May 2026 the tourist ETA is free of charge for German nationals (previously a paid category); extensions are described as extremely time-consuming and should be arranged with the Department of Immigration and Emigration in advance.
fee_notes: Free of charge for German citizens as of 25 May 2026 (a change from the earlier USD 50 fee).

conditions_text: German citizens do not need a visa for entry and stay in Turkey of up to 90 days within any 180-day period. The previous practice of leaving for a single day to reset a new 90-day period is no longer permitted, and visa-free entry does not guarantee an absolute right of admission.

German citizens holding a valid biometric passport do not need a visa for tourism, business (without taking up employment), or visit purposes in the UAE, for up to 90 days within any 180-day period. The passport must be valid for at least six months from the date of entry.
Singaporeans may enter Armenia visa-free for short stays of up to 180 days from the date of initial entry within a 12-month period.
Singaporeans can visit Colombia for up to 90 days for tourism without a visa.
Singaporeans can visit Costa Rica for up to 180 days without a visa for tourism; the exact length of stay granted is determined by the immigration officer (Migración) on arrival.
Citizens and stateless persons permanently residing in Singapore may enter and stay in Georgia without a visa for up to one full year (365 days) per entry.
Singapore passport holders may enter Indonesia visa-free for tourism under the A1 Visa Exemption for up to 30 days; this visa-free stay cannot be extended.
Singaporeans receive a free visa on arrival for up to 30 days, provided they hold an onward/return ticket and proof of sufficient funds or a confirmed accommodation booking.
fee_notes: Free of charge for the initial 30 days; can be extended for up to a total of 90 days for a fee (approx. 750 MVR for the extension).

conditions_text: Singaporeans can visit Mexico for up to 180 days without a visa, provided no employment is pursued during the stay.
Singaporeans can visit Peru for tourism for up to 90 days without a visa.

Singapore passport holders may enter the Philippines visa-free for up to 30 days for tourism, provided they hold a return/onward ticket and a passport valid at least 6 months beyond the intended stay; longer stays require an extension from the Bureau of Immigration.
Singaporeans can visit Serbia for up to 90 days within a 180-day period from the date of initial entry, without a visa.

Under a bilateral reciprocal agreement between Sri Lanka and Singapore, Singapore nationals must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) before arrival, valid for 30 days with double-entry from the date of first arrival.
fee_notes: ETA is processed free of charge for Singapore nationals under the reciprocal agreement (in effect since 25 May 2026); extensions beyond 30 days require payment of the applicable visa fee.

conditions_text: Singapore passport holders do not require a visa for visits of less than 90 days within any 180-day period to Türkiye for social/tourist visit purposes.
Singapore passport holders can stay visa-free for up to 90 days in the UAE within a 180-day period, with entry stamped on arrival and no advance visa application needed.

Brazilian passport holders (all passport types) may enter Armenia without a visa for stays of up to 180 days, under Armenia's bilateral visa-waiver agreement with Brazil, per Armenia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs list of countries with a visa-free regime under bilateral/multilateral agreements.

Brazilian nationals do not need a visa for tourism, business, or transit; a Permiso de Turismo (PT) of up to 90 days is granted on arrival, and a valid Brazilian national ID card can substitute for a passport under the CAN/Mercosur framework.
Brazil is classified in Group 1 of Costa Rica's official visa directive (Directrices Generales de Visas), which allows entry without a visa for up to 180 calendar days, generally non-extendable.
Brazil is on Georgia's official visa-exemption list, and Brazilian passport holders may enter and remain in Georgia for up to 365 days without a visa.

Since 3 July 2025, under Minister of Immigration and Corrections Regulation No. 9 of 2025, Brazilian citizens can enter Indonesia visa-free for tourism for up to 30 days. An electronic Visa on Arrival (e-VOA) remains available as an alternative and can be extended once for a further 30 days.
fee_notes: Free under the visa-exemption route; the alternative e-VOA costs about IDR 500,000 (roughly USD 32) if chosen instead.

conditions_text: Brazilian passport holders receive a free 30-day tourist visa on arrival, provided they show proof of onward travel, prepaid accommodation, and sufficient funds, plus complete the online IMUGA Traveller Declaration before arrival.
fee_notes: Free of charge on arrival; extensions of up to a further 60 days (90 total) are possible for a fee.

conditions_text: As of 5 February 2026, Mexico requires Brazilian nationals to hold a visa. A new fully-online electronic visa (visa electrónica) is available for a single entry by air only, for visitors not engaging in paid activities; it does not replace the traditional consular visa, which remains required for land/sea entry or multiple entries.
fee_notes: Traditional multi-entry consular visitor visa costs about USD 56 (2026 rate) and is valid up to 180 days; the electronic visa's fee and exact authorized stay were not specified in the official announcement.

conditions_text: As a Mercosur-associated nationality, Brazilian citizens can enter Peru without a visa for tourism; total stay as a visa-exempt tourist is capped at 183 cumulative days within any rolling 365-day period, under Legislative Decree No. 1350 (Migration Law).

Under a bilateral exchange of notes between the Philippines and Brazil on reciprocal abolition of non-immigrant visa requirements, Brazilian passport holders may enter and stay in the Philippines visa-free for 59 days — longer than the standard 30-day allowance most nationalities receive.
Brazilian ordinary passport holders do not need a visa for tourism or business and may stay up to 90 days within any 6-month period counted from the date of first entry.

Since October 2025, Sri Lanka requires all visitors, including Brazilians, to obtain an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) online before departure. Brazil is not among the roughly 40 nationalities granted the ETA free of charge, so the standard fee applies; the ETA permits a 30-day stay.
fee_notes: Standard ETA fee of approximately USD 50, paid online at the official eta.gov.lk portal.

conditions_text: Brazilian passport holders may enter Turkey without a visa for tourism or business, for up to 90 days within any 180-day period, under a visa-exemption arrangement in place since 2004.

Under a bilateral visa-waiver agreement between Brazil and the UAE in force since 2018, Brazilian ordinary, official, and diplomatic passport holders may enter the UAE without a visa and stay up to 90 days within any 12-month period. A passport valid for at least 6 months is required; the exemption does not cover paid work or study, which require separate authorization.

Japan is not on India's visa-exemption list, so Indian passport holders must obtain a visa before travel. Since the JAPAN eVISA system was extended to India, tourists can apply for a single-entry short-term stay eVisa entirely online through a Ministry of Foreign Affairs-accredited agency (VFS Global) rather than visiting an embassy in person; a traditional paper visa application through a Japanese consulate remains an alternative option.

US passport holders do not need a visa for short-term stays (tourism, business meetings, visiting friends/family) of up to 90 days. A passport valid for the duration of the stay and proof of onward/return travel may be requested at immigration. Note: Japan's new electronic pre-travel authorization system, JESTA, is expected to become mandatory for currently visa-exempt nationalities including the US by 2028, but is not yet in effect.

British Citizen passport holders do not need a Temporary Visitor visa for tourism, visiting friends/relatives, or short business trips of up to 90 days, under the Japan-UK visa exemption arrangement. Paid activity is not permitted under this status. Note: Japan's upcoming JESTA electronic travel authorization system, expected by 2028, will apply to UK travelers once in force.

Canadian passport holders do not need a visa for tourism or short-term business purposes for up to 90 days, under the Japan-Canada bilateral visa exemption agreement. A passport valid at least 6 months beyond the intended departure from Japan and proof of onward/return travel are expected at immigration. Note: starting around 2028, Canada and other currently visa-exempt nationalities will need to register in advance through Japan's new JESTA electronic travel authorization system.

Australian passport holders do not need a visa for tourism, business, or transit for stays of less than 90 days. Travelers are photographed and fingerprinted on arrival, and must complete an arrival card. Note: Japan's planned JESTA electronic travel authorization system, expected by 2028, will extend to Australian travelers once implemented.

German passport holders do not need a visa for short-term stays (tourism, business meetings, transit) of up to 90 days under Japan's visa exemption arrangements. Paid activity is not permitted under Temporary Visitor status. Note: Japan's forthcoming JESTA electronic travel authorization system, expected by 2028, will apply to German travelers once in force.

Singapore passport holders do not need a visa for short-term entry (tourism, family visits, unpaid activities) of less than 90 days. Working or freelancing for a Japanese company is not permitted on this Temporary Visitor status. Note: Japan's upcoming JESTA electronic travel authorization system, expected by 2028, will extend to Singapore travelers once implemented.

Under the Brazil-Japan reciprocal visa waiver arrangement (in force since 30 September 2023), holders of a valid Brazilian ICAO-compliant e-passport can enter Japan visa-free for short-term stays (tourism, business, family visits, short-term activities) of up to 90 days; paid work or exercising a profession is excluded. The arrangement, originally set to expire 30 September 2026, was extended via an exchange of diplomatic notes (published in Brazil's Diario Oficial da Uniao on 29 July 2026) through 29 September 2029.

Effective 15 September 2026, Thailand's revised visa exemption scheme (published in the Royal Gazette 31 August 2026) added India to the 30-day visa-exemption list for tourism, replacing India's previous visa-on-arrival status. Entry is limited to tourism purposes. All travelers, regardless of nationality, must also submit Thailand's Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online within 72 hours before arrival.
fee_notes: No fee for the visa-exempt entry itself; a one-time 30-day extension is available at a Thai immigration office for roughly 1,900 THB. TDAC submission is free on the official government portal (tdac.immigration.go.th).

conditions_text: Brazil has a long-standing bilateral visa exemption agreement with Thailand for holders of ordinary passports, granting up to 90 days visa-free for tourism. conditions_text: No visa is needed for a visit, but a USA passport holder must hold an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) before travelling to the UK. British citizens (the UK passport categories IRCC lists, e.g. British citizen) are visa-exempt for Canada but need an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) to fly to or transit through a Canadian airport. You do NOT need an eTA when arriving by car, bus, train or boat (including a cruise ship), but you still need a valid passport. With a valid eTA you can make repeated short visits, normally for up to six months at a time; the officer at the border decides the length of each stay. Apply only on the official Canada.ca site. IRCC's list names UK passport categories rather than 'United Kingdom' as a single entry, so check that your passport category is on the eTA list.

conditions_text: India is NOT on the DHA visa-exemption list (issued 09 December 2025): the list shows 90 days only for diplomatic, official and service passports, with the ordinary-passport column blank, so an ordinary Indian passport needs a visa or authorisation before travel. Two routes exist today. (1) ETA, in force now: South Africa's Electronic Travel Authorisation (official portal eta.dha.gov.za; launched officially 12 August 2026). India was one of the four original pilot nationalities (China, India, Indonesia, Mexico) named in the Minister's launch speech on gov.za, and the portal says holders of valid ordinary passports may apply online provided they will land at OR Tambo (Johannesburg), Cape Town, Lanseria or King Shaka airport. For visa-required travellers the ETA is issued as a port-of-entry visa (Section 10(a)); it is valid up to about 6 months, multiple entry, each stay up to 90 days, and the DHA says most outcomes arrive within 24 hours. The launch speech says the ETA will 'progressively become compulsory' for short stays from visa-required countries; I found no published compulsory start date for India, so treat it as the official online route and do not arrive without either an approved ETA or a visa. (2) Traditional visa: the South African High Commission in New Delhi states that all visa applications are lodged through VFS Global and that it does not accept applications directly; this route also covers arrival at any port other than the four ETA airports. Catches: the ETA FAQ says your passport must be valid for at least 7 months from your intended travel date, fees are non-refundable even if refused, an approved ETA does not guarantee entry, and a yellow-fever certificate is required if you arrive from a risk country. Carry return/onward ticket, accommodation and funds proof. Since 1 July 2026 all travellers must also complete the SARS online traveller declaration before entering or leaving.
fee_notes: The ETA fee amount is not stated on the DHA ETA pages checked; it is shown in the portal before you pay, and all ETA fees are non-refundable whether or not the application succeeds. VFS Global visa fees were not verified from an official page.

conditions_text: No visa needed: the Department of Home Affairs visa-exemption list (issued 09 December 2025, marked subject to change without notice) lists this nationality as exempt on ordinary passports for stays of up to 90 days, with no visa fee. Passport: the DHA says it must be valid for at least 30 days after the end of your intended visit and have at least one unused page for entry/departure endorsements; UK FCDO advises at least 2 blank pages, so carry 2. The Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA) launched officially on 12 August 2026 at four airports (OR Tambo, Cape Town, Lanseria, King Shaka), but for visa-exempt travellers it is voluntary: the DHA ETA FAQ says visa-exempt travellers may travel without one and are processed under standard immigration procedures, so it is NOT required for this passport today. Catch: since 1 July 2026 every traveller entering or leaving South Africa must also complete the SARS online traveller declaration (a customs declaration, not a visa) before travelling. Carry a return or onward ticket, proof of accommodation and proof of funds, as the immigration officer can ask for these at the port of entry. A yellow-fever certificate is needed if you arrive from a yellow-fever-risk country. Special requirements apply for travellers aged 17 and under; check the DHA.

India is not on Korea's list of K-ETA-exempt countries (the Korean mission list names Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Macao, Canada, the US, Guam, 15 European countries and Australia and New Zealand) and Indian passport holders must obtain a Korean visa in advance through the Korea Visa Portal (visa.go.kr): fill in the e-Form online, print it and submit it in person at the KVAC-VFS visa application centre (the Chennai embassy page says Indian nationals 'must apply for Korean Visa and obtain it through the Visa Portal'). For tourism the usual category is the short-term tourist visa (C-3-9) described on Korean embassy pages. K-ETA is for visa-free nationalities and is not the route for Indian passport holders. The length of stay is set on the visa issued, so max_stay_days is left null. Catch: Korea runs a separate visa-free scheme for Jeju Island for nationals of visa-required countries who fly directly to Jeju from overseas (not via Seoul or Busan); the Korean mission notice (April 2026) lists 23 excluded nationalities and India is not among them. The Indian Embassy in Seoul (advisory of 24 February 2026) says the Jeju facility is for short-term tourism only, does not cover mainland Korea and does not guarantee entry: immigration officers at Jeju airport decide, and it advises carrying printed return ticket, hotel booking for the full stay, itinerary, proof of funds and a passport valid at least six months. A trip that continues to Seoul or Busan needs the visa.

No visa needed for tourism or business of up to 90 days (stated in the US State Department's South Korea advisory; travel.state.gov blocked automated fetching, so that figure was read through a search result rather than an opened page). A K-ETA is normally required for visa-free entry, but US citizens are on the temporary K-ETA exemption list: the Korean consulate notice (Dallas, opened) says the exemption runs 1 January to 31 December 2026 (KST) and covers the US. The exemption is temporary: Korea's Ministry of Justice has extended it a year at a time, the current period ends on 31 December 2026 (KST), and nothing seen says what happens on 1 January 2027, so check k-eta.go.kr before booking any trip that starts in 2027 or later. Exempt travellers may still apply for a K-ETA voluntarily (KRW fee applies) to skip the arrival card. Previously issued K-ETAs stay valid to their expiry date. Work or paid activity needs a visa.

The Korean embassy in Singapore states Singapore passport holders are exempt from K-ETA until 31 December 2026, and that there is no requirement on the passport's remaining validity as long as it stays valid throughout the stay in Korea. Brazilians do not need a visa for tourism, business, family visits or events of up to 90 days, but they must obtain a K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) before boarding, and it is in force today. Brazil is not on the K-ETA temporary exemption list (the list is Japan, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, Macao, Canada, US, Guam, 15 European countries, Australia and New Zealand), so the requirement applies now. Brazil's foreign ministry (MRE) states the K-ETA is mandatory for stays of up to 90 days and that a visa is needed for stays of more than 90 days; the Korean embassy in Brazil says the K-ETA does not replace a visa, must be applied for at least 72 hours before travel on the official site k-eta.go.kr only (many look-alike sites charge more), and that a denied applicant cannot reapply successfully unless circumstances change significantly. The K-ETA guide on k-eta.go.kr states the fee is KRW 10,000 and processing is generally within 72 hours. The Korean embassy also says travellers who only visit Jeju on a direct flight do not need a K-ETA, but anyone planning to visit other regions needs one before entering Jeju.
